source_note: Praetor 500/600 systems study for the Praetor FO study (SIMCOM initial Sep 29, 2026). One entry per Flexjet Crew Training Handbook Rev 2.5 §7 'Systems Review Questions' section (24 sections), mapped to the AOM chapter its answers cite. cards = every §7 question with its CTH answer (formatting cleanup only; AOM references moved out of the answer into cite, typos like 'AOM 9-10350' kept as printed). Duplicate questions printed twice in the CTH (e.g. 7.5 q05/q20, 7.20 q58–61/q89–92) are kept. summary_points are distilled only from those answers (the one exception cites CTH §6 p.20) and cite the card ids. mel_notes from Praetor MEL Rev 14 (02-17-26); ob_notes from Embraer OB P550-001/23. No AOM was available: the AOM references are as cited by the CTH and haven't been checked against the AOM. CTH page numbers = printed pages. 7.24 tables were rebuilt by hand from a two-column layout.

cards.q: What is the length of the Praetor 500 and Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 = 64' 7" Praetor 600 68' 0.5"

cards.q: What is the height of Praetor 500? Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 = 21" 3" Praetor 600 21' 0.3"

cards.q: What is the wingspan of the Praetor 500 and Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 = 70' 6.4" Praetor 600 70' 6.4"

cards.q: What is the minimum pavement width for a 180* turn?
cards.a: Praetor 500 – 52'5" Praetor 600 - 56'

cards.q: How should the cockpit seats be adjusted?
cards.a: Vertically and then/after using the black and white spheres.

cards.q: Is there an internal storage compartment?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Where is the internal storage compartment accessed?
cards.a: Through a door in the lav.

cards.q: What is the normal configuration for the cockpit?
cards.a: Dark and quiet.

cards.q: What does an illuminated white striped bar on a button mean?
cards.a: That it is not in its normal position.

cards.q: How many identical Display Units (DU) are there?
List the three different types of windows that can be displayed on the DU's?
cards.a: Primary Flight Displays (PFD), Multifunction Displays (MFD) and Crew Alerting System (EICAS)

cards.q: What are the three pilot selectable format window sizes for the MFW's?
cards.a: ¼ size, ½ size and full size.

cards.q: Which Display Unit(s) DU will be available in the event of an electrical emergency?
cards.a: Only the CTR DU will be available.

cards.q: How long can the In-Flight Entertainment (IFE) take to be fully operational after its power up?
cards.a: 15 minutes.

cards.q: Where is the emergency exit located?
cards.a: Over the right wing forward of the lavatory or in the lavatory.

cards.q: What are the 5 doors that are depicted on the STATUS synoptic page?
cards.a: Main Cabin Door, Cargo Compartment Door, Emergency Exit Door, Fuel Door and the Electronic Bay Door.

cards.q: What are the emergency equipment items onboard the aircraft?
cards.a: Flashlights, life vests, life rafts, fire extinguishers, a crash axe, smoke goggles, an ELT, crew and pax O2 and a first aid kit.

cards.q: What does a continuously flashing red LED light on the ELT cockpit control panel indicate?
cards.a: The ELT is active.

mel_notes.text: Fixed ELT may be inoperative (deactivated) or missing ('ELT not Installed' placard in view of the pilot), with repairs within 90 consecutive calendar-days (Cat A).

summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.23 (citing AOM 9-09-50) [cards q04]

cards.q: How is the FDR recording accomplished?
cards.a: Automatically.

cards.q: What is the FDR recording and for how long?

cards.q: Does the CVR record both written communications exchanged via datalink and cockpit audio communication?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: How are CVR operations accomplished?
cards.a: Automatically.

cards.q: How much water is each potable water system capable of carrying?
cards.a: 3.96 gallons.

cards.q: How are the potable water tanks filled?
cards.a: Manually with a funnel through a service panel.

cards.q: What temperature of water is recommended to fill the galley and lavatory potable water tanks?
cards.a: Hot water not exceeding 35*C\95*F.

cards.q: How can the potable water system be drained?
cards.a: By pressing the water drain button on the overhead panel.

cards.q: How long can the potable water tanks take to drain if the tanks are full of water?
cards.a: Up to 10 minutes.

cards.q: At what waste tank capacity does the Cabin Management System indicate the necessity of servicing?
cards.a: When the tank is 85% full.

cards.q: When servicing the waste system, how long should rinse water be supplied through the servicing cart to clean the waste tank?
cards.a: For three minutes.

cards.q: When should the waste and potable water system be drained to avoid damages to their components caused by water freezing??
cards.a: During operation in cold weather below 0*C more than one hour.

mel_notes.text: Galley potable water system may be inop if drained and placarded DO NOT SERVICE.

summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.23 (citing AOM 9-01-40) [cards q01, q02, q03, q04]

summary_points.text: Red beacon = visual indication of engine operation.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-01-40) [cards q05]

summary_points.text: Wing inspection light illuminates the left-hand wing leading edge.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-01-40) [cards q06]

summary_points.text: Cargo lights: manual switch by the cargo door, on for five minutes.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-01-40) [cards q07]

summary_points.text: Dome lights are the cockpit light available in an electrical emergency.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-01-40) [cards q08]

cards.q: What lights are included in the courtesy lights?
cards.a: The entrance dome light and lights installed in each step of the stairs.

cards.q: How can the courtesy lights be turned on?
cards.a: The courtesy lights are turned on by pressing a momentary switch installed on the main door entrance sidewall and remain lighted for 5 minutes.

cards.q: Once the main door switch is pressed, how long will the courtesy light remain illuminated?
cards.a: 5 minutes.

cards.q: What bus are the courtesy lights powered by?
cards.a: The HOT BUS.

cards.q: Which light is used as a visual indication of engine operation?
cards.a: The red beacon light.

cards.q: What part of the aircraft does the wing inspection light illuminate?
cards.a: The left hand leading edge of the wing.

cards.q: How are the cargo compartment lights turned on and for how long?
cards.a: Through a manual switch by the cargo door for five minutes.

cards.q: Which cockpit light is available during an electrical emergency condition?
cards.a: The dome lights.

cards.q: What are the emergency lights powered by?
cards.a: Two exclusive NiCad batteries.

cards.q: When will the emergency lights automatically turn on with the EMER LT knob in the ARMED position?
cards.a: If the main DC busses lose power due to electrical emergency condition or impact on the airplane.

cards.q: How are the emergency lights controlled?
cards.a: Via the emergency lighting button on the overhead panel.

mel_notes.text: Overwing emergency lights may be inop provided operations are not conducted at night.

summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-15-30; AOM 9-15-40) [cards q01, q02, q06]

summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.24 (citing AOM 9-15-40) [cards q11, q12]

summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-15-40) [cards q14]

cards.q: What buttons will illuminate red when a warning CAS message appears in the EICAS window?
cards.a: The WARN buttons.

cards.q: What buttons will illuminate amber when a warning CAS message appears in the EICAS window?
cards.a: The CAUT buttons.

cards.q: How is it indicated on the EICAS that there is a checklist to complete with an associated CAS message?
cards.a: A box is displayed next to the CAS message.

cards.q: What symbol is displayed to indicate that an EICAS checklist has been completed?
cards.a: A check mark will be drawn in the box next to the CAS message.

cards.q: List the four EICAS priority levels.
cards.a: WARNING (red), CAUTION (amber), ADVISORY (cyan) and STATUS (white).

cards.q: How should all warning and caution CAS messages be acknowledged by the pilots?
cards.a: By pressing either the master warning (WARN) or master caution (CAUT) buttons.

cards.q: Can CAS messages be cancelled so long as the activation condition still exists?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Give the standard definition for OFF that is used for all systems.
cards.a: The system is still available just turned off.

cards.q: Give the standard definition for FAIL that is used for all systems.
cards.a: The system is unavailable and there is a total loss of system functionality.

cards.q: Give the standard definition for FAULT that is used for all systems.
cards.a: The system performance is degraded but the system is still available.

cards.q: What is an EICAS message that generates more than one CAS message called?
cards.a: A "Golden" CAS message.

cards.q: How is a "golden" CAS message indicated?
cards.a: By a preceding chevron >.

cards.q: Are some CAS messages inhibited on takeoff or approach and landing to prevent them from becoming a nuisance?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Where are time-critical warnings annunciated?
cards.a: On the PFD 1 and PFD 2.

cards.q: Which button allows the aural alerts on the respective side to be inhibited?
cards.a: The AURAL MUTE button.

cards.q: What voice message is generated when the airplane configuration is suitable for takeoff after the TO CONFIG button is pressed?
cards.a: TAKEOFF OK.

cards.q: List the items that will activate the takeoff aural warning whenever the airplane is on the ground and thrust is applied.
cards.a: Flaps not in takeoff position, parking brake set, any spoiler panel is deployed or if the pitch trim is out of the green range.

cards.q: Will a terrain overlay pop up on the HSI whenever a TAWS alert becomes active?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: When TCAS issues an RA, what kind of an indication will the pilot have indicating a "fly to" zone?
cards.a: A green box.

cards.q: List the four EICAS priority levels.
cards.a: WARNING (red), CAUTION (amber), ADVISORY (cyan) and STATUS (white).

mel_notes.text: Master WARNING/CAUTION lights and alarm-cancel functions: 2 installed, 1 required each.

summary_points.text: 28 V DC generation and distribution; with both generators available they operate split bus.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-05-01) [cards q01, q02]

summary_points.text: GPU white AVAIL = button out, GPU connected, 25–30 V DC; green IN USE when pushed in and powering the airplane.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-05-30) [cards q03, q04]

summary_points.text: Two 24 V DC 40 Ah NiCad main batteries; BATT 2 feeds the APU START BUS.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-05-40; AOM 9-05-55) [cards q14, q15, q21]

summary_points.text: APU generator: on the ground powers all loads including shed buses; in flight all loads except the shed buses. Two generators are needed for the shed buses in flight.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 pp.25, 26 (citing AOM 9-05-40; AOM 9-05-55) [cards q09, q10, q22]

summary_points.text: Electrical emergency (in flight) = both main generators and the APU generator unavailable; RAT deploys automatically.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-05-40) [cards q12, q13]

summary_points.text: RAT powers EMER BUS 1, 2 and 3 and charges the batteries; right-seat pilot can pull the red manual deploy control.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-05-30; AOM 9-05-40) [cards q08, q11]

summary_points.text: Batteries only in flight: EMER buses powered and red BATT DISCHARGING CAS.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-05-40) [cards q16]

summary_points.text: EMER BUS 1/2/3 can be powered by BATT 1, BATT 2 or the RAT.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-05-55) [cards q18]

summary_points.text: With no power source, only HOT BATT BUS 1 and 2 are energized.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-05-55) [cards q19]

summary_points.text: Ground servicing with GPU button out and batteries OFF energizes SHED BUS 1.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-05-55) [cards q20]

summary_points.text: Battery voltage shows amber when discharging; RAT only shown on synoptic when deployed and powering.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.25 (citing AOM 9-05-30) [cards q05, q07]

cards.q: What type of an electrical system is the airplane equipped with?
cards.a: A 28 V DC electrical power generation and distribution system.

cards.q: If both generators are available, do they operate in a split bus mode or parallel mode?
cards.a: Split bus mode.

cards.q: What does the white AVAIL light indicate?
cards.a: That the GPU button is pushed out, a GPU is connected and the voltage is set between 25V DC and 30 V DC.

cards.q: Which light will illuminate when the GPU button is pushed in and providing power to the airplane?
cards.a: If the GPU button is pushed in and providing power to the airplane the white AVAIL light will go off and the green IN USE light will illuminate.

cards.q: What color does the battery voltage indication show if the battery is discharging?
cards.a: Amber.

cards.q: What will the indication be on the electrical synoptic page if the GPU is connected but is not providing power to the airplane?
cards.a: A white GPU.

cards.q: Will the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) be continuously displayed on the electrical synoptic page? If not, when will it be displayed?
cards.a: No, only when it is deployed and providing power to the airplane.

cards.q: How can the pilot manually command the RAT to deploy?
cards.a: The right seat pilot can pull the red manual deploy control.

cards.q: What buses is the APU capable of supplying power to on the ground if the APU is the only source of electrical power?
cards.a: All electrical loads including the shed buses and charging the batteries.

cards.q: What buses are the APU capable of supplying power to inflight?
cards.a: All electrical loads (except for the shed buses) and charging the batteries.

cards.q: What buses does the RAT generator power?
cards.a: EMER BUS 1, 2 and 3 and charging the batteries.

cards.q: When will the RAT automatically deploy?
cards.a: During an electrical emergency.

cards.q: In flight, when will an electrical emergency occur?
cards.a: When the two main generators and the APU generator are unavailable.

cards.q: How many main batteries are there?
cards.a: Two.

cards.q: What is the rating of the main batteries?
cards.a: 24 V DC 40 Ah NiCad batteries.

cards.q: If the batteries are the only source of electrical power inflight, what buses will be powered and what CAS message will be displayed?
cards.a: The EMER BUSES; the red BATT DISCHARGING CAS message.

cards.q: In an electrical emergency, what buses are powered/isolated from the aircraft electrical system?
cards.a: EMER BUS 1, EMER BUS 2 and EMER BUS 3.

cards.q: In an electrical emergency, what sources of power can provide electrical power to the EMER BUS 1, EMER BUS 2 and EMER BUS 3?
cards.a: BATT 1, BATT 2 or the RAT.

cards.q: What buses will be energized when the airplane is de-energized and there is no electrical power source available?
cards.a: HOT BATT BUS 1 and HOT BATT BUS 2.

cards.q: For ground servicing, when a GPU is connected and providing power to the airplane, with the GPU button pushed out and the BATT 1 and BATT 2 switches in the OFF position, which bus in energized by the GPU?
cards.a: SHED BUS 1.

cards.q: Which battery is connected to the APU START BUS to assist with an APU start?
cards.a: BATT 2.

cards.q: How many generators need to be operating in order for the SHED BUSES to be energized in flight?
cards.a: Two.

mel_notes.text: One main DC generator may be inop (Cat B): gen OFF, APU generator operative and used throughout the flight, pump 2A operative, no contaminated runways, at or below 31,000 ft. (Pre-mod SB 550-29-0002: only GEN 1 relief.)
APU DC generator may be inop (Cat C) if selected OFF and both main DC generators are operative.
GPU AVAIL/IN USE lights inop: verify capable GPU by white GPU pictorial and at least 27.5 V before pushing GPU in.

summary_points.text: FUEL XFEED knob OFF for takeoff, landing and go-around.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-10-30; AOM 2-36) [cards q01]

summary_points.text: No wing-to-wing transfer; crossfeed lets both engines and/or the APU feed from one tank.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-10-50) [cards q05, q06]

summary_points.text: Each tank: two DC pumps (main A, backup B) and two scavenge pumps. A pump controlled by the engine ECU, B pump by the FCU.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-10-50) [cards q08, q09, q10]

summary_points.text: B pump comes on automatically for engine start, APU start on the run, fuel low pressure, or A-pump failure.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-10-50) [cards q11]

summary_points.text: FUEL LEAK SUSPECTED: > 880 lb difference for 5 min. FUEL WING IMBALANCE: > 510 lb.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 pp.26, 27 (citing AOM 9-10-50; AOM 9-10-500) [cards q07, q12]

summary_points.text: Total fuel quantity in red triggers aural 'FUEL' twice.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.26 (citing AOM 9-10-30) [cards q04]

summary_points.text: P600 FWD/VTRL aux tanks transfer automatically to both wings simultaneously, never to each other; not during XFEED, takeoff, go-around or landing. Manual: select FWD or VTRL on FUEL TRANSFER panel.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.27 (citing AOM 9-10-50; AOM 9-10-30; AOM 9-10350) [cards q21, q22, q23, q24]

summary_points.text: Refuel by gravity or pressure; defuel by suction and/or pressure. P600 aux tanks also gravity-refuelable.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.27 (citing AOM 9-10-50) [cards q18, q19, q20]

summary_points.text: Max fuel tank temperature for takeoff 52 °C.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.27 (citing AOM 2-36) [cards q27]

summary_points.text: Capacity per §7.7: P500 13,146 lb total / 13,058 usable; P600 16,262 / 16,138 (these differ from CTH p.17; see limitations conflicts).
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.27 [cards q25, q26]

cards.q: When must the FUEL XFEED knob be set to OFF?
cards.a: For takeoff, landing and go around.

cards.q: Which MFD page provides a visual representation of the fuel system operation and parameters?
cards.a: The FUEL synaptic page.

cards.q: What color does the total and individual tank quantities and fuel temperature indications indicate when in the normal operating range?
cards.a: Green.

cards.q: When the total fuel quantity is displayed in red, which aural warning is played twice?
cards.a: FUEL.

cards.q: Can fuel be transferred from one wing to the other?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How does the cross-feed valve allow corrections in the event of a fuel load imbalance?
cards.a: It allows both engines and/or the APU to be fed by one tank.

cards.q: Which CAS message is displayed on the EICAS when the difference between the current and expected fuel quantities is higher than 880 lb. for 5 minutes?
cards.a: The amber FULE LEAK SUSPECTED CAS.

cards.q: How many fuel pumps does each fuel tank have?
cards.a: Two DC fuel pumps {Main (A) and back up (B)} and two scavenge pumps.

cards.q: What controls the main (A) pump when the fuel pump is in the AUTO position?
cards.a: The engine ECU.

cards.q: What controls the backup (B) pump when the fuel pump is in the AUTO position?
cards.a: The FCU.

cards.q: List the four times when the backup (B) pump will be automatically commanded on when the fuel pump is in the AUTO position.
cards.a: During engine start, APU start on the run, fuel low pressure detection and when the main (A) pump fails.

cards.q: When will the amber FUEL WING IMBALANCE CAS message be displayed on the EICAS?
cards.a: When the fuel imbalance between the tanks is higher than 510 pounds.

cards.q: Where is the pressure refueling point and REFUELING/DEFUELING control panel located at?
cards.a: Forward portion of the right wing fuselage.

cards.q: How long does the system pre-check on the REFUELING/DEFUELING panel take to verify fuel system operation?
cards.a: Approximately 10 seconds.

cards.q: Which switch located on the REFUELING/DEFUELING control panel enables pressurized refueling to be performed with the airplane energized by either the APU/GPU or battery power?
cards.a: The power selection switch.

cards.q: What should happen if the STOP REFUEL is displayed on the REFUELING/DEFUELING control panel during the refueling process?
cards.a: The process shall be halted manually by the operator by moving the refueling switch to the OFF position.

cards.q: Can the tanks be refueled using the gravity refuel port on the top of each wing?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: What are the two different methods that the airplane can be refueled?
cards.a: By gravity or pressure.

cards.q: What are the two different methods that the airplane can be defueled?
cards.a: By suction and/or pressure.

cards.q: Can the FWD and VRTL tanks in the Praetor 600 be refueled via gravity?
cards.a: Yes, via refuel ports on the right hand side of each aux tank.

cards.q: How is fuel transferred from the FWD or VTRL tanks and where?
cards.a: Automatically to both wings simultaneously.

cards.q: Can fuel be transferred from the FWD/VTRL tanks to each other?
cards.a: No, only to the wings.

cards.q: If the AUTO function of the fuel panel for the FWD/VTRL tanks fail, how do we access the remaining fuel?
cards.a: By selecting either FWD or VTRL on the FUEL TRANSFER panel.

cards.q: When is TRANSFER operations from the FWD or VTRL tanks not allowed?
cards.a: During XFEED operation, takeoff, go-around and landing operations.

cards.q: What is the total fuel capacity of the Praetor 500 and the Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 = 13,146 lbs. Praetor 600 = 16,262

cards.q: What is the total usable fuel for the Praetor 500 and the Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 = 13,058 lbs. Praetor 600 = 16,138

cards.q: What does the TEST button on the FIRE PROTECTION panel test?
cards.a: The smoke detection system and it checks only the cockpit visual and aural indications.

cards.q: If the APU is running, two consecutive fire TESTS within what time period may cause the APU to shut down?
cards.a: 15 seconds.

cards.q: Is the engine fire detection system continuously monitored?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: How many fire bottles does the engine fire extinguishing system have?
cards.a: Two.

cards.q: Which systems are Bottle A and Bottle B used for?
cards.a: Bottle A is dedicated to the engines and Bottle B is dedicated to the engines and the APU.

cards.q: List the 4 things that happen when the SHUTOFF 1 (2) button is pushed on the ENGINE FIRE panel.
cards.a: They close the associated fuel, hydraulic and bleed shut off valves plus the Bottle A and Bottle B buttons are illuminated to indicate that they are armed.

cards.q: What happens when the APU SHUTOFF button is pushed in?
cards.a: It closes the APU fuel and bleed shut off valves plus it arms the fire bottle B.

cards.q: Will the APU automatically shut down if a fire or overheat condition is detected on the ground?

cards.q: What happens when the CARGO button on the FIRE PROTECTION panel is pressed in flight?
cards.a: In flight, pressing the CARGO button immediately discharges the high-rate fire extinguisher bottle into the cargo compartment and starts a two-minute timer to discharge the metered bottle.

cards.q: What happens when the CARGO button on the FIRE PROTECTION panel is pressed on the ground?
cards.a: On the ground, pressing the CARGO button immediately discharges the high-rate fire extinguisher bottle into the cargo compartment. A second push of the CARGO button is required to discharge the metered bottle.

cards.q: What are the two different sizes for the low rate (metered) extinguisher bottle?
cards.a: Either 78 minutes or 110 minutes.

cards.q: How can a pilot identify which size of a low rate (metered) extinguisher bottle is on their aircraft?
cards.a: It is placarded in the cargo compartment.

cards.q: Does the internal stowage compartment have fire detection/protection? If so, what?

cards.q: What services does the APU provide and what are they used for?
cards.a: An electrical generator supplies 28 V DC to the electrical system. The pneumatic power is used for engine starting and to supply bleed air to the air-conditioning pack of the environmental system (ECS).

cards.q: How is the APU controlled and monitored?
cards.a: Through a dedicated Full Authority Digital Electronic Control unit (FADEC).

cards.q: What does pressing the APU ON/OFF button do?
cards.a: It starts the ECU power-up sequence and initiates the APU built-in test (BIT).

cards.q: When does the START button on the APU CONTROL panel flash green?
cards.a: During the ECU bit test.

cards.q: What does the START button on the APU control panel illuminating steady green indicate?
cards.a: The APU is ready to start.

cards.q: If the START button on the APU control panel illuminates amber what does that indicate?
cards.a: The APU start in inhibited.

cards.q: What are the APU starter limitations?
cards.a: Up to three consecutive unsuccessful start attempts are allowed with 30 second intervals between attempts.

cards.q: What MFD page can APU information be seen on?
cards.a: The STATUS synoptic page.

cards.q: Which tank normally supplies fuel to the APU?
cards.a: The right tank.

cards.q: Is it possible to feed the APU from the left wing tank? If so, how?
cards.a: Yes, via the cross-feed system.

cards.q: Can the APU supply bleed air on the ground or in flight?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: If the APU is the only source of electrical power on the ground, what buses can the APU power?
cards.a: All of the airplane electrical loads and charge both batteries.

cards.q: If the APU is the only source of electrical power in flight, what buses can the APU power?
cards.a: All electrical loads (except for the SHED BUSES) and also charging both batteries.

cards.q: What is the APU operating envelope for starting, operation and to supply electrical power?
cards.a: Up to 31,000 feet.

cards.q: Up to what altitude is the APU able to supply bleed air for engine starting?
cards.a: Up to 23,000 feet.

cards.q: Where does the APU get its power for starting?
cards.a: The number two battery.

cards.q: What should be displayed on the STATUS synoptic page if the APU oil quantity is sufficient?
cards.a: A green "OK"

cards.q: List the 4 conditions that will cause the APU to automatically shut down either in flight or on the ground.
cards.a: Overspeed, under speed, ECU internal failure or an APU bleed leak.

cards.q: List the conditions that will cause the APU to automatically shut down on the ground only.
cards.a: APU fire, APU EGT over temperature, APU high oil temperature, APU low oil pressure, APU starter not engaged or an APU fuel shut off valve failure.

cards.q: How many Full Authority Digital Electronic Controls (FADEC) does each engine have?
cards.a: Two single channel FADEC's.

cards.q: Where are the engine indications and alerts displayed?
cards.a: On the engine indication and crew alerting system (EICAS).

cards.q: Which position of the ignition selector knob allows the FADEC to control the ignition system depending on engine requirements.
cards.a: Auto.

cards.q: Which thrust lever position provides the maximum thrust rating available for dual or single engine operation?
cards.a: MAX.

cards.q: Which thrust lever position selects the takeoff and go-around thrust and mode settings?
cards.a: TO/GA.

cards.q: What does pressing the EVENT MARKER button cause the ECU (FADEC) to do?
cards.a: Records a total of three minutes (two minutes before pressing the event button and one minute after the event marker button is pressed.

cards.q: When is the OAT on the EICAS indication displayed?
cards.a: Up until the takeoff run.

cards.q: What are the thrust reversers used for and during what phase of flight?
cards.a: An on-ground additional braking device used for the landing and RTO only.

cards.q: Is backing up the airplane with reverse thrust allowed?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Upon landing when should the thrust reversers be stowed?
cards.a: At 40 kts.

cards.q: When are the thrust reversers available?
cards.a: With WOW signal indicating that the airplane is on the ground and a wheel speed.

cards.q: What icon on the EICAS indicates the current status of the thrust reverser?
cards.a: A REV icon.

cards.q: What color icon indicates that the thrust reversers are commanded and in transition?
cards.a: An amber REV icon.

cards.q: Where is the IGNITION status displayed?
cards.a: On the EICAS.

cards.q: What does a green IGN indicate?
cards.a: The ignitions are commanded on.

cards.q: What icon on the EICAS indicates that the igniters are commanded to OFF?
cards.a: A cyan IGN OFF.

cards.q: Where can the oil level be accurately read?
cards.a: Either in the sight glass or measured via the Remote Oil Level Sensor (ROLS).

cards.q: When can the oil level be accurately read?
cards.a: From 5 to 30 minutes after shutdown.

cards.q: Is the engine oil quantity indication visible with an engine running or in flight?
cards.a: No it isn't.

cards.q: What is the maximum oil consumption rate of the engine per hour?
cards.a: 0.04 quarts per hour (or one quart per 25 hours).

cards.q: List the three sources of air pressure that the Air Turbine Starter can use for an engine start.
cards.a: The APU, an opposite engine or a ground air supply (huffer cart).

cards.q: What is the purpose of the Automatic Takeoff Thrust Control System (ATTCS)?
cards.a:
To provide automatic thrust increase if the ATTCS is previously armed and any one of the following conditions is true on takeoff or go-around:
• OEI condition is detected (N2 difference between engines is greater than 15%)
• Loss of engine cross communication.
• Wind shear is detected.
• Thrust lever is moved to the MAX position.

cards.q: When is the ATTCS function available?
cards.a: When WAI is ON "ICE PROT" mode knob is in "ALL"

cards.q: Which takeoff ratings may be selected by the flight crew prior to takeoff?
cards.a: The full rated mode (T-O1) and the one de-rated mode (TO-2).

cards.q: List the engine power settings that may be selected by the flight crew.
cards.a: Take off/Go-Around (TO/GA), maximum continuous (CON), climb (CLB), cruise (CRZ) and maximum reverse (for landing or a rejected takeoff).

cards.q: What are the starting and motoring limitations?
cards.a: Max accumulated time – five minutes; Max consecutive cycles – three; after reaching five minutes of accumulated time or three cycles (whichever occurs first), combining consecutive engine starting in motoring, 15 minutes of cool down time is required prior to an additional engine start motoring.

cards.q: What are the starting duty cycle limits?
cards.a: Maximum time of 80 seconds.

cards.q: How many consecutive starts are allowed before a cooling time of 15 minutes is required prior to additional starts or motoring?
cards.a: Three.

cards.q: Can the engine be started with an ITT above 450*C? If so, what must be accomplished prior to start?
cards.a: Yes, dry motor the associated engine for 30 seconds prior to start.

cards.q: When can HP thermal bow occur? If an engine restart is desired within that period of time, what is the recommended procedure?
cards.a: When engine starts are initiated between 15 and 180 minutes after an engine shutdown. Dry motor the associated engine prior to start for 15 seconds or until N2 reaches 23% (whichever occurs first). After completion of this procedure, a normal engine start sequence can be initiated any time after 3 minutes and before 40 minutes have elapsed.

cards.q: How many hydraulic systems are there?
cards.a: Three.

cards.q: What nominal pressure do all three hydraulic systems operate at?
What MFD page provides a visual representation of the hydraulic system operation and parameters?

cards.q: What pressure is an amber tick mark placed at on the pressure indication for all three systems on the hydraulic synoptic page.
What color is the symbol for shutoff valves that are open, engine driven pumps that are on and hydraulic flow lines that are pressurized?
cards.a: Green.

cards.q: Will a failure of two hydraulic systems result in a complete loss of flight-critical functions?
cards.a: No, due to system design.

cards.q: What is hydraulic system 1 comprised of?
cards.a: One reservoir, one engine driven pump (EDP1), one electrical DC motor pump (DCMP1), one shutoff valve (SOV 1) and on accumulator.

cards.q: When will the DCMP 1 be automatically commanded on with the HYD 1 ELEC PUMP knob in the AUTO position?
cards.a: During takeoff and landing phases.

cards.q: What is hydraulic system 2 comprised of?
cards.a: One reservoir, one engine driven pump (EDP 2), one shut off valve (SOV 2) and one accumulator.

cards.q: What is hydraulic system 3 comprised of?
cards.a: One reservoir, one electrical DC motor pump (DCMP 2) and one accumulator.

cards.q: Hydraulic system 3 is designed to operate in conjunction with what electrical system (s)?
cards.a: The battery and the ram air turbine (RAT).

cards.q: What is the only source of hydraulic power for hydraulic system 3?
cards.a: The electric DCMP 3.

cards.q: What is the source of electrical power for the electric DCMP 3 (hydraulic system 3)?
cards.a: EMER BUS 3.

cards.q: If the airplane loses any 2 of the 3 hydraulic systems due to overheat, will the overheat protection system still be functional on the remaining system?
cards.a: No, it will be inhibited.

cards.q: What is the backup for hydraulic systems 1 and 2?
cards.a: The PTU.

cards.q: What is the primary function of the PTU?
cards.a: To transfer power from hydraulic system 1 to system 2 or vice versa.

cards.q: When the PTU knob is in the AUTO position, when will the LGHCU's automatically activate the PTU?
cards.a: In the event of an engine failure or EDP failure.

cards.q: What type of flight control system does the aircraft have?
cards.a: A functionally distributed Fly-by-Wire (FBW) control system.

cards.q: What are the two basic modes of operation for the flight controls?
cards.a: Normal mode (NM) and direct mode (DM).

cards.q: When will the flight control system revert automatically to Direct Mode (DM) operations?
cards.a: When it is not possible to keep the normal mode (NM) operation due to multiple system failures.

cards.q: Is flight under Direct Mode (DM) recommended? Why or why not?
cards.a: No, it should be avoided as some airplane protection functions are only available in normal mode (NM)

cards.q: What happens when the AP/PTY button is momentarily pressed?
cards.a: The auto pilot is automatically disengaged.

cards.q: What happens when the AP/PTY button is pressed for more than 1 second?
cards.a: Exclusive control is given to the side stick while pressed in the priority annunciation is activated.

cards.q: What happens when the AP/PTY button is pressed and held for more than 20 seconds?
cards.a: The perspective side stick will have exclusive control latched.

cards.q: If one sidestick has been latched out, how can exclusive control be removed?
cards.a: By pressing either side's priority button.

cards.q: What happens if dual sidestick input occurs and priority has not been requested by either pilot?
cards.a: A tactile warning and both sidesticks is activated and an oral warning and PFD flag are triggered. The sidestick inputs are algebraically summed.

cards.q: Is sidestick controller priority logic available in Direct Mode?
cards.a: No, it's only available in normal mode (NM).

cards.q: With the autopilot engaged, what does pressing the Touch Control Steering (TCS) button do?
cards.a: It allows the pilot to manually control the airplane while the autopilot is engaged.

cards.q: During manual flight with flaps 3 or full, landing gear down and the AP disengaged, what does pressing the Touch Control Steering (TCS) button do?
cards.a: It resets the TCS trim speed bug.

cards.q: How can the multifunction spoilers be deployed for use as speed brakes?
cards.a: By the speed brake lever.

cards.q: What are the angles of multifunction spoilers that correspond with the speed brake positions?
cards.a: From 0* (STOW) to 30* (FULL).

cards.q: When can the Pitch Trim Switch be manually commanded?
cards.a: Only on the ground or in direct mode (DM).

cards.q: Which button is used to recover Normal Mode (NM) or to revert to Direct Mode (DM) in the case of a Normal Mode (NM) misbehavior?
cards.a: The FLTCTRL NORMAL MODE button.

cards.q: When is a manual reversion to Direct Mode (DM) inhibited?
cards.a: When the following FCS protection envelopes are engaged: Low speed protection, Angle of Attack (AOA) limiter protection and high-speed protection.

cards.q: On the FLIGHT CONTROL synoptic page, what color actuator status indicates that the respective flight control surface is in the normal mode and at least one actuator is engaged?
cards.a: Green.

cards.q: On the FLIGHT CONTROL synoptic page, what does a yellow actuator status indicate?
cards.a: It indicates direct mode and at least one actuator is operational.

cards.q: When is the side slip target presented by a blue side slip skid indicator?
cards.a: In one engine inoperative (OEI) condition during takeoff, climb or go-around flight phase.

cards.q: Where is the Low Speed Awareness (LSA) band located? The Pitch Limit Indicators (PLI's)?
cards.a: Adjacent to the speed tape; on the ADI.

cards.q: List the three LSA bands in NORMAL MODE (NM) and what they indicate.
cards.a:
Vss – top of the white tape – low speed protection function.
Vaoa – Top of the amber tape – AOA limiter function activation.
Vlim – Top of the red tape – the speed associated with the maximum allowable AOA airspeed.

cards.q: Do the Vss and Vaoa/Vlim indications behave the same in turns and other maneuvers? Why or why not?
cards.a: No, because the Vss is defined in terms of speed and Vaoa/Vlim are defined in terms of AOA.

cards.q: Do Vaoa and Vlim increase with load factor?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Is the AOA limiter function operational in Direct Mode (DM)?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: List the two LSA bands in Direct Mode (DM) and what they represent.
cards.a:
Vms – top of the amber tape.
Vsa – Top of the red tape, indicates the airspeed at which the stall aural alert is triggered.

cards.q: Are the Pitch Limit Indicators (PLI's) displayed in Direct Mode (DM)?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What color does the Pitch Limit Indicator become if the airspeed drops below Vaoa in Normal Mode (NM)? How about Vlim?
cards.a: Amber, Red.

cards.q: How many Flight Control Computers (FCC's) are sufficient to provide Normal Mode (NM) functionality?
cards.a: One.

cards.q: What is the purpose of the Black Airplane Battery?
cards.a: To withstand operation for a minimum of 15 minutes in order for the flight crew to recover the proper airplane to electrical system operation.

cards.q: How long does each PBIT test of the FCS take?
cards.a: Less than one minute.

cards.q: If the PBIT conditions are not satisfied, up to how many PBIT operation attempts can the FCS automatically perform?
cards.a: Up to three.

cards.q: During PBIT operation, which CAS message is displayed?
cards.a: The FLITCTRL TEST IN PROGRESS CAS.

cards.q: When is the de-rotation control law active?
cards.a: When the airplane touches down.

cards.q: What does the neutral spiral stability control law provide?
cards.a: It automatically trims the elevator when the sidestick controller is set back to the neutral position to maintain flight level during turns up to 33* of bank angle.

cards.q: If the pilot commands a turn with a bank angle of greater than 33*, what do they need to do in order to maintain level flight in that turn?
cards.a: Maintain the desired sidestick lateral deflection and move the sidestick controller aft.

cards.q: List the 4 conditions that will cause the speed brakes to automatically stow.
cards.a: If the airspeed drops below 160 knots or the TLA position is greater than 55*, the flap level and position is set to 3 or full, or the AOA limiter is engaged.

cards.q: If the speed brakes are automatically stowed, what indication will the pilots have and how can the speed brakes be reactivated?
cards.a: The cyan SPDBRK LEVER DISAG CAS message is displayed and the SPEED BRAKE LEVER must be set back to stow.

cards.q: How is manual reversion to Direct Mode (DM) available if the flight crew detects a Flight Control Normal Mode (NM) misbehavior?
cards.a: By pressing the FLIGHT CONTROLS Normal Mode button.

cards.q: What do the Flight Control Laws (CLAWS) provide?
cards.a: Flight envelope protections to prevent the airplane from exceeding the flight limit envelope limitations.

cards.q: What are the two flight envelopes for the airplane?
cards.a: The normal flight envelope and the limit flight envelope.

cards.q: What are the limits of the normal flight envelope?
cards.a: 33* bank angle protection, high speed protection (Vmo), low-energy avoidance protection (1.13 Vs) and pitch attitude protection.

cards.q: What are the limits of the high-speed protection envelope?
cards.a: The airspeed is limited to Vmo +22 kts.

cards.q: When does the pitch attitude protection activate?
cards.a: At pitch angles of 30* pitch up and 15* pitch down.

cards.q: What does the limit flight envelope require?
cards.a: More effort to maintain the airplane in this configuration.

cards.q: What are the boundaries/hard limits of the limit flight envelope?
cards.a: The external boundaries of the limit flight envelope are reached at full control application. The hard limits of the limit flight envelope are the maximum AOA, airplane structural limits (load factor protection), maximum sideslip protection, and dive speed protection. There are no hard limits for pitch and bank angles.

cards.q: Is the AP operational in Direct Mode (DM)?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: In Direct Mode (DM), how does the airplane behave?
cards.a: Like a conventional airplane and the sidestick controller and pedal deflections are directly related to the surface position.

cards.q: What systems make up the Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS)?
cards.a: The flight director (FD), autopilot (AP) and the auto throttles (AT).

cards.q: Which panel hosts the controls for the AP, AT and FD, plus lateral and vertical reference /mode selection and course selection?
cards.a: The Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS) panel.

cards.q: What does pushing the FD button on the AFCS panel do?
cards.a: Engages and disengages the flight director on those PFD's.

cards.q: What does pushing the AT button on the AFCS panel do?
cards.a: Engages and disengages the auto throttle.

cards.q: What does the outer ring of the SPD knob do?
cards.a: Select the source of the speed reference between MAN and FMS.

cards.q: What does pushing the HDG button on the AFCS panel do?
cards.a: Select heading mode when pushed once and alternates with roll mode is pushed again.

cards.q: Pushing the BANK button on the AFCS will toggle between what bank angles?
What is the up and down range of the FPA mode?
cards.a: 9.9* up and down.

cards.q: How can the flight path angle/reference line be selected?
cards.a: By rotating the FPA knob.

cards.q: What does the outer knob of the ALT knob select? The inner knob?
cards.a: Selects the altitude increasing/decreasing 1000 feet. Select the altitude increasing/decreasing 100 feet.

cards.q: What does pushing the SRC button do?
cards.a: Alternates between PFD 1 and PFD 2 FMA modes as the source for the auto pilot.

cards.q: When the autopilot is engaged, what does pushing the TCS button on the sidestick do?
cards.a: It activates the TCS (AP override) as long as neither the takeoff nor go-around mode is active.

cards.q: Where are the AT/DISC buttons located? The TO/GA buttons?
cards.a: On the thrust levers.

cards.q: With the AP engaged, will the AP disengage if the force is applied on the sidestick, either in the pitch or roll direction?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: What are the two FD cues presented?
cards.a: The flight director cue (a magenta circle) and the takeoff cross bar.

cards.q: What does the green Flight Path Vector cue indicate?
cards.a: The current flight path in reference to the horizon line.

cards.q: Where is the Flight Mode Annunciator (FMA) located and what does it display?
cards.a: On the upper part of both PFD's; annunciation for auto throttle, autopilot, approach status, lateral and vertical modes.

cards.q: List the FMA color codes for normal operation.
cards.a:
Magenta – For FMS active/engaged modes.
Green – Non-FMS active/engaged modes.
White – Armed modes;
Amber – Alert condition
Red – Abnormal condition.

cards.q: What does an amber LIM on the FMA indicate?
cards.a: The auto throttle is in speed mode and the selected speed target cannot be achieved because the auto throttle has limited N1 rating.

cards.q: What are the two precision approach capabilities of the airplane?
cards.a: Either APPR 1 or APPR 2.

cards.q: When is the autopilot aural alert triggered?
cards.a: When the auto pilot is disengaged by the pilot or due to a system failure.

cards.q: How can the autopilot aural alert be cancelled?
cards.a: By pressing AP/PTY buttons on either side stick.

cards.q: When will the airplane automatically transition to the half bank mode?
cards.a: When the aircraft altitude is greater than 25,000 feet during a climb.

cards.q: Prior to selecting the TO/GA button, what must be set in order to display the takeoff crossbar on the PFD?
cards.a: The flaps set to 1 or 2, the aircraft weight must be set and the takeoff speeds must be sent in the FMS.

cards.q: What computed takeoff speed reference is set in T/O mode?
cards.a: V2 + 15 kts (AEO); in the case of OEI below V2 the speed reference will be set to V2.

cards.q: What altitudes are associated with the ILS approach check points to try to engage the highest system capability available?
cards.a: 1500 ft RA and 800 ft RA.

cards.q: What is Emergency Descent Mode (EDM)?
cards.a: A function than can automatically bring the airplane to a safe altitude in the ultimate scenario of cabin depressurization and pilot incapacitation.

cards.q: When is EDM enabled?
cards.a: When the autopilot is engaged and the aircraft is above 25,000 ft.

cards.q: When is EDM activated?
cards.a: When EDM is enabled and a depressurization event occurs (a red CABIN ALTITUDE CAS message is displayed)

cards.q: If the autopilot (AP) is engaged, what happens to the auto throttle (AT) when the airspeed is below the top of the LSA white bar?
cards.a: The auto throttle will automatically be engaged.

cards.q: What happens to the Autopilot (AP) when the AOA limit function is activated?
cards.a: It is disengaged.

cards.q: What phases of flight is the auto throttle system approved to operate in?
cards.a: All phases of flight; takeoff, climb, cruise, descent, approach, landing and during OEI operations.

cards.q: What is the purpose of the HOLD mode of the auto throttle?
cards.a: To ensure that no undesirable thrust reductions are experienced during the takeoff.

cards.q: When will the auto throttle (AT) HOLD mode be activated?
cards.a: From the time the airplane exceeds 60 kts during the takeoff until 400 ft AGL.

cards.q: What is the minimum autopilot engagement height?
What is the minimum autopilot use height with Vertical Path Reference?
cards.a: 80 ft.

cards.q: What is the minimum autopilot use height without Vertical Path Reference?
When planning to land with the auto throttle engaged, what is the Vref additive and how much is unfactored landing distance multiplied by?
cards.a: 5 kias; 1.1.

cards.q: How many oxygen cylinders supply oxygen to both crew and passengers?
cards.a: One.

cards.q: When will the passenger oxygen masks automatically deploy with the OXYGEN knob in PAX AUTO?
cards.a: If the cabin altitude exceeds 14,500 ft (+/- 300 ft.)

cards.q: What are the two capacities of oxygen bottles available?
cards.a: 77 liters and 115 liters.

cards.q: Where are the oxygen system parameters and indications displayed?
cards.a: On the STATUS synoptic page.

cards.q: What are the selections that can be toggled between on the MODE SELECTOR on the oxygen mask?
cards.a: N (normal mode), 100% and EMGCY.

cards.q: What position must the MODE SELECTOR be set to in order to stow the oxygen mask?
What is the purpose of the OXYGEN SAVER PUSH-PULL BUTTON on the oxygen mask?
cards.a: To allow the crew to breath cabin air when the oxygen supply is not required.

cards.q: Which mode can the OXYGEN SAVER PUSH-PULL BUTTON be pushed in?
cards.a: Only in the N (normal) mode.

cards.q: What does the oxygen pressure in green indicate?
cards.a: It is in the normal range of operation.

cards.q: What does the oxygen pressure in white indicate?
cards.a: It is an advisory operating range and the oxygen dispatch pressure charts must be referenced for the minimum pressure to dispatch.

cards.q: How many smoke goggles are provided?
cards.a: One for each flight crewmember.

cards.q: Can smoke or toxic fumes be purged from the smoke goggles? How?
cards.a: Yes, by the vent valve.

cards.q: The oxygen mask is designed to be donned within how many seconds?
cards.a: Five Seconds.

cards.q: When must the OXYGEN SAVER PUSH-PULL BUTTON be manually closed?
cards.a: In case of fire or smoke.

cards.q: Does the oxygen mask need to be removed from the stowage box to be tested?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How is the oxygen mask tested?
cards.a: Turn on the Comm Panel Speaker select, then press both the PRESS TO TEST AND RESET button on the LH door and the PRESS TO TEST button on the regulator simultaneously for 1 second (ensure the FLOW INDICATOR goes out during the test which leak-tests the inflation hose and airflow can be heard into the mask) and the mic can be heard through the speakers.

cards.q: When must the Oxygen Cylinder Toggle switch not be set to ON?
cards.a: When the ambient temperature is below -15 *C.

cards.q: What does pulling the LANDING GEAR FREE FALL LEVER do?
cards.a: Relieves the hydraulic pressure in the landing gear lines and mechanically releases the uplock hooks for all the landing gear.

cards.q: What does it mean when the LANDING GEAR POSITION INDICATIONS turn to red icons?
cards.a: That more than 20 seconds has passed since a discrepancy has been detected between the landing gear lever position and the actual landing gear position.

cards.q: If the parking brake is not fully released on the ground, what CAS message will be displayed?
cards.a: Either a white PARKING BRAKE ON CAS or a cyan CHECK PARKING BRAKE CAS message.

cards.q: If the parking brake is not fully released in flight, what CAS message will be displayed?
cards.a: An amber PARK BRAKE NOT REL CAS message.

cards.q: Where can the emergency/park brake accumulator pressure and the brake temperature indications be seen?
cards.a: On the STATUS synoptic page.

cards.q: How long can the light on the STEERING button and the STEERING DISC CAS message take to go off after the first engagement of the nose wheel steering?
cards.a: Up to two seconds.

cards.q: Which steering switch has priority for safe operation on the ground?
cards.a: The external STEERING DISENGAGE switch.

cards.q: When will the green TOWING ALLOWED light in the external steering panel illuminate?
cards.a: When the external STEERING DISENGAGE switch is in the DISENGAGE position and the parking brake in not applied.

cards.q: How far should the airplane be towed slowly in a straight line before turning?
cards.a: 10 feet.

cards.q: When should the DN LCK REL (down lock release) button be used?
cards.a: Only in the event of a landing gear control lever failure or when it is necessary to clear obstacles.

cards.q: What type of brake system is on the aircraft?
cards.a: Brake-by-wire.

cards.q: During normal operations, what does the Brake Control Unit (BCU) provide?
cards.a: Locked wheel protection, anti-skid protection, gear retract braking, touchdown protection, a gear extension test, brake temperature monitoring and auto brake (optional).

cards.q: Where can the Brake Temperature Monitoring System (BTMS) information be found an what does it provide?
cards.a: On the STATUS synoptic page, brake temperature status on the synoptic page and brake overheat warning on the EICAS.

cards.q: Where must the brake temperature indication be prior to takeoff?
cards.a: In the green range.

cards.q: What are the two different modes of AUTOBRAKE control?
cards.a: Landing mode (LO, MED, HI) and rejected takeoff (RTO).

cards.q: What kind of pressure will autobrake in the RTO mode apply?
cards.a: A brake pressure equivalent to the maximum manual braking.

cards.q: When will autobrake applications begin on landing?
cards.a: Autobrake application will start one second after WOW indicates ground and thrust levers signal at idle.

cards.q: Is antiskid protection available while braking with the emergency /parking brake?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What handle position is used when using the emergency/parking brake as a parking brake?
cards.a: The handle must be pulled until it locks at the full up position.

cards.q: Where can the emergency/parking brake handle be set to as a reference for emergency braking?
cards.a: To the intermediate position (first detent).

cards.q: How can the emergency /parking brake be modulated?
cards.a: By keeping the release button pressed.

cards.q: How many full applications/how many hours of parking do the emergency/parking brake accumulators provide?
cards.a: 6 full or 16 hours.

cards.q: When the airplane is airborne, is the steering system engaged?
cards.a: No, it will automatically be disengaged.

cards.q: What is the maximum range that the nose wheel can turn in free wheel steering mode?
List the steering angles and associated speed with nose wheel steering engaged:
cards.a: Steering angle varies from +/- 62* up to 10 kts, decreasing laterally to +/- 8* at 25 kts and then to +/- 3* at 68 kts.

cards.q: What airspeed is Vlo?

cards.q: List the items that use bleed air.
cards.a: Environmental control system (ECS), engine start, engine wing and horizontal stabilizer anti-icing system, cargo heating system (optional) and main cabin door pressurization seal.

cards.q: When is the cabin temperature control transferred to the VIP seat panel?
cards.a: When the detect C is selected to the PAX CABIN TEMPERATURE CONTROL KNOB.

cards.q: In the event of a bleed leak detection, what light will illuminate in addition to an associated CAS message?
cards.a: The PACK, BLEED 1, BLEED 2 or APU BLEED the amber light.

cards.q: When is the Outflow Valve (OFV) indication on the Environmental Control System (ECS) synoptic page displayed?
cards.a: It is only available on the ground.

cards.q: What are the potential sources of bleed air that the Pneumatic System Controller (PSC) can automatically select from?
cards.a: Engines, the APU and external connections.

cards.q: Is it possible to have bleed from the APU and the engines simultaneously?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: During normal operation on the ground and for taxiing, what is the primary source of bleed air?
cards.a: The APU.

cards.q: What is the primary source of bleed air in flight?
cards.a: The engines.

cards.q: When will the bleed air source be automatically transitioned to the engines?
cards.a: When the airplane starts running for takeoff (engines TLA's higher than 50 degrees)

cards.q: The XBSOV (cross bleed shut off valve) is automatically commanded to close for what conditions?
cards.a: In case of bleed leakage, over pressure, engine fire or if a failure condition is identified.

cards.q: Can an external ground connection be used to supply pressurized air for an engine start?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: If an external pneumatic power source is being used and is not adjustable, what range should the pressure supply be in?
cards.a: Between 32 psi and 60 psi.

cards.q: When is fast cooling enabled on hot days?
cards.a: When the difference between the cockpit/cabin temperature set point and the cabin/cockpit zone temperature is equal to or higher than 6* C.

cards.q: When is fast warming enabled on cold days?
cards.a: When the difference between the cockpit/cabin temperature set point and the cabin/cockpit zone temperature is equal to or higher than 6* C.

cards.q: What happens to the recirculation fan during fast cooling and fast warming operations?
cards.a: It automatically sets a higher speed to optimize system performance.

cards.q: If the air conditioning pack fails what does the PSC automatically do?
cards.a: It engages the pack backup operational mode and controls cabin and cockpit temperature.

cards.q: What is ram air ventilation used for?
cards.a: Non-pressurized flight or for smoke evacuation.

cards.q: When will the PSC command the emergency RAM air door to open?
cards.a: In case of loss of the air condition PACK and the PACK backup systems.

cards.q: How can the emergency RAM air door be manually commanded to open?
cards.a: Through the DUMP button on the PRESSURIZATION control panel.

cards.q: How is the Cargo Heating System operated?
cards.a: Automatically by the PSC.

cards.q: When is the main cabin door pressurized seal inflated?
cards.a: After takeoff.

cards.q: How can the outflow valve be modulated?
cards.a: Either automatically or manually.

cards.q: What position are the Negative and Positive Pressure Relief Valves (NPRV and PRV) normally in?
cards.a: Closed.

cards.q: What does pushing in the MODE selector button on the PRESSURIZATION panel allow for?
cards.a: Manual control of the pressurization system through the CABIN ALT knob.

cards.q: What is the cabin altitude rate of change when moving the CABIN ALT knob UP or DN?
cards.a: 50 FPM steps.

cards.q: What happens when the DUMP button is pressed in the automatic mode of operation?
cards.a: The cabin is depressurized at a constant rate of change of 2,000 ft/min up to 12,000 ft and the emergency RAM air door is opened.

cards.q: What happens when the DUMP button is pressed in the manual mode of operation?
cards.a: The cabin rate of change will increase with the duration of the dump command; until either the command is removed or the altitude limit function disables it when the cabin altitude reaches 14,800 ft +/- 200 ft. The emergency RAM door air is also opened.

cards.q: What is the maximum differential pressure for a 6,000 ft cabin altitude? For a 5,800 ft cabin altitude?
cards.a: 9.64 psid; 9.73 psid

cards.q: What is the maximum differential overpressure?
cards.a: 10.4 psid.

cards.q: What is the maximum differential negative pressure?
cards.a: 0.5 psid.

cards.q: What is the maximum differential pressure for takeoff and landing?
cards.a: .02 psid.

mel_notes.text: Automatic pressurization control inop: manual control verified, at or below FL250. Manual control inop: at or below 15,000 ft (with auto operative).
Air conditioning pack inop: unpressurized at or below 9,500 ft, ram air door secured open, ground ops with door closed ≤ 30 min (P600 Cat A, 10 flight-days/60 flight-hours).

Pack backup inop: selected OFF, SOV secured closed, cooling pack operative, at or below FL250 (-01 also within 60 min of a suitable airport; -02 ram air door secured open). CAS PACK FAULT: dispatch if pack backup is operative.
mel_notes.cite: MEL Rev 14 item 21-53-00 (p. 21-25); MEL Rev 14 Section Two CAS relief item 2-18 (printed footer CAS-C-13)

mel_notes.text: One engine bleed inop: at or below FL200 (or FL250 with no known/forecast icing), within 60 min of a suitable airport, crossbleed operative if Bleed 1 affected.

Cross-bleed valve inop: selected OFF and secured closed except for left engine start; at or below FL200 (-01, single bleed SOV confirmed open before flight in icing) or FL250 with no known/forecast icing (-02); within 60 min of a suitable airport. In-flight left engine start: AFM windmilling start procedure.

summary_points.text: Icing: OAT (ground/takeoff) or TAT (flight) 10 °C or below with visible moisture.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 2-50) [cards q02]

summary_points.text: ICE SPEED RESET only per checklist when certain there is no ice; it resets LSA to non-icing and removes STALL PROT ICE SPEED.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 2-50; AOM 9-12-30) [cards q04, q05]

summary_points.text: APU bleed isn't used for ice protection (ground tests only). Engine anti-ice uses engine hot air; wing/stab uses pneumatic hot air.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q07, q08, q09]

summary_points.text: Two ice detectors, left and right nose.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q11]

summary_points.text: Windshield heat is electric; power-saving mode on a single DC source; inoperative on battery.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q12, q13, q14]

summary_points.text: XBLEED closed + right bleed lost = single bleed operation (max 20,000 ft); XBLEED closed + left bleed lost = anti-ice inoperative.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50; AOM 2-50) [cards q17, q18, q19]

summary_points.text: Takeoff selector: ENG at 5–10 °C with moisture, ALL below 5 °C with moisture, otherwise AUTO.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q20]

summary_points.text: In ALL for takeoff, A-I WINGSTAB ARMED goes to ON at TLA > 59° and wheel speed > 30 kt.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 p.40 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q21]

summary_points.text: AUTO mode activates above 1,700 ft AGL or 2 min airborne, whichever first; wing/stab turns off 2 min after icing is no longer detected.
summary_points.cite: CTH Rev 2.5 pp.40, 41 (citing AOM 9-12-50) [cards q22, q23]

cards.q: What sub-systems does ice and rain protection include?
cards.a: Wing and stabilizer anti-ice systems; engine anti-ice systems, ADSP/TAT heating system; windshield heating system and windshield and rain protection system.

cards.q: When may icing conditions exist?
cards.a: Whenever the OAT on the ground or for takeoff or TAT in flight is 10*C or below and visible moisture in any form is present.

cards.q: Where can performance data/limits for operations in icing conditions be found?
cards.a: In the performance section and/or OPERA.

cards.q: When may the ICE SPEED RESET position on the ICE PROTECTION panel be selected?
cards.a: In accordance with the checklist, only if the crew is certain that there is no ice accretion on the airplane.

cards.q: What does the ICE SPEED RESET position on the ICE PROTECTION MODE do?
cards.a: It resets the stall protection (LSA bands) to non-icing condition settings and removes the STALL PROT ICE SPEED CAS message.

cards.q: When is the APU icon and associate flow line on the ICE PROTECTION synoptic page displayed?
cards.a: On the ground only.

cards.q: Can the APU bleed be used as a bleed source for ice protection?
cards.a: No, except for ground tests.

cards.q: How does the Engine Anti-Ice system protect the engine air inlets from ice formation?
cards.a: By extracting hot air from the engines.

cards.q: How does the Wing and Stabilizer Anti-Ice System protect the wing and stabilizer leading edges from icing formation?
cards.a: It uses hot air from the pneumatic system.

cards.q: How can the Wing and Horizontal Stabilizer Ice Protection Systems test be initiated?
cards.a: By pressing the ice protection TEST button on the ICE PROT panel.

cards.q: How many ice detectors are on the airplane and where are they located?
cards.a: Two; left and right side of the nose section.

cards.q: How does the Windshield Heating System (WHS) protect the windshield from ice and fog formation?
cards.a: It uses electrical power to heat the windshield.

cards.q: When will the WHS operate in a power savings mode?
cards.a: If the airplane system is fed by a single DC source.

cards.q: Does WHS operate if the system is fed by battery power?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: How are the ADSP/TAT probes heated?
cards.a: Electrically.

cards.q: Will the Anti-Ice system monitor icing condition and automatically activate in all flight phases?
cards.a: Yes.

cards.q: Whenever the XBLEED is closed and the right bleed source is not available, the anti-ice system is in?
cards.a: Single bleed operation.

cards.q: What is the maximum operating altitude for anti-ice single bleed operations?
Whenever the XBLEED is closed and the left bleed source is not available, the anti-ice system is?
cards.a: Inoperative.

cards.q: List the 3 ICE PROTECTION MODE knob settings/temperatures for takeoff.
cards.a: ENG if the visible moisture is between 5C and 10C with visible moisture; ALL if the temperature is lower than 5*C with visible moisture; and AUTO for all other conditions.

cards.q: If the MODE knob is in ALL for takeoff, when will the white A-I WINGSTAB ARMED CAS message go to white A- I WINGSTAB ON?
cards.a: When the TLA is greater than 59 degrees and the wheel speed is greater than 30kts.

cards.q: When the ICE PROT MODE knob is in the AUTO position and the ice detector recognizes the icing condition, at what point will the ice protection system be activated in flight?
cards.a: Whenever the airplane is above 1,700 ft AGL or 2 minutes in the air whichever occurs first.

cards.q: When will the wing and stabilizer anti-ice system automatically be turned off after the airplane leaves icing conditions?
cards.a: Two minutes after icing is no longer detected.

mel_notes.text: Wing/stab anti-ice inop: WINGSTAB OFF, AISOV secured closed, no known/forecast icing.
One engine anti-ice inop: no known/forecast icing, affected side OFF and valve confirmed closed.
One ice detector inop: operate anti-ice manually (ENG 5–10 °C, ALL < 5 °C on ground; ALL if TAT < 10 °C with moisture in flight). Both inop: no known/forecast icing.

cards.q: What provides the flight crew with the interface to control the audio functions of all radio communication and navigation systems?
cards.a: The Audio Control Panel.

cards.q: Where are the antennas for the VHF 1, VHF 2 and VHF 3 located respectively on the fuselage?
cards.a: VHF1 and VHF3 are on Top and VHF2 is on bottom.

cards.q: What services can the optional VHF 3 provide?
cards.a: Voice and data link capability, like ACARS and CPDLC.

cards.q: If the TUNE knob on the RSP is in the NORM position, list some of the ways frequencies can be tuned:
cards.a: Via the CCP, via the MKP or the MFW TUNING window.

cards.q: What does the HF communication system provide?
cards.a: Long range air-to-air, air-to-ground and ground-to-air communication.

cards.q: What is SELCAL used for?
cards.a: It is a ground to air calling system that relieves the flight crew from having to continuously monitor the VHF and HF communications radios.

cards.q: Where is the ramp audio jack located?
cards.a: On the lower LH portion of the forward fuselage. It is part of the STEERING DISENGAGE/RAMP INTERPHONE panel.

cards.q: Where does left MKP tuning enter frequencies into?
cards.a: #1 (NAV and COM)

cards.q: Where does right MKP tuning enter frequencies into?
cards.a: #2 (NAV and COM).

cards.q: What does pushing the microphone select button on the Audio Control Panel (ACP) do?
cards.a: Selects the microphone audio and makes the selection to the active transmitter.

cards.q: What do the audio control knobs on the ACP do?
cards.a: Provides for selection and volume control of the associated received audio signal.

cards.q: What does the HDPH knob on the ACP do? The SPKR knob?
cards.a: Controls headphone volume. Controls the selection of the speaker on/off and the volume for the flight deck speakers.

cards.q: Can the volume of the aural voice and tone warnings to the speaker be adjusted by the SPKR knob on the ACP?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What does the BOOM/AUTO/MASK knob on the ACP in the AUTO position allow for?
cards.a: The oxygen mask microphone to be automatically selected when the oxygen mask is donned and switches back to boom when the oxygen mask is properly stowed.

cards.q: What does the VOX knob on the ACP do?
cards.a: Provides on/off and sensitivity control for the voice-activated interphone.

cards.q: What does the ST knob on the ACP do?
cards.a: Controls the side tone volume in the selected radio.

cards.q: What does pushing the AUDIO BACKUP button on the AUDIO JACK PANEL do?
cards.a: It recovers the use of the onside radio when full ACP functionality is not available.

cards.q: What does pushing the AURAL MUTE button on the AUDIO JACK PANEL do?
cards.a: It inhibits the aural alerts on the respective side and displays the cyan AVXN AURAL WARN 1 (2) OFF CAS message.

cards.q: Where are the PTT buttons located at for each pilot?
cards.a: One momentary PTT button on the CCP, one momentary PTT button on the sidestick controller and one 3- way position slide switch on the glare shield.

cards.q: What are the switch positions for the TUNE knob on the RSP?
cards.a: COM 1(2), 121.5, NORM and L(R) MKP ONLY.

cards.q: If MKP ONLY is selected without a display tuning (RTSA) failure, what message will be displayed over the tuning window?
cards.a: LEFT/RIGHT SIDE DISPLAY TUNING INHIBITED.

cards.q: If the crew receives a new ACARS message, how will they be alerted?
cards.a: By a cyan ACARS MESSAGE CAS.

cards.q: Can you rely on ADF indications on the PFD while transmitting in HF?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: What selection needs to be activated on the COM 3 control page prior to using CPDLC?

cards.q: How will a pilot be notified that an uplink (CPDLC) message has arrived?

cards.q: Does an ATC message received have priority over an ACARS message received?

cards.q: What is the usage of ATN-CPDLC restricted to?

cards.q: What phase of flight is the usage of ATN-CPDLC restricted to?
