cards.q: What color is the active target speed bug and the active target speed indication when MAN is set on the SPD knob on the AFCS panel? When FMS is set on the SPD knob?
cards.a: Cyan / magenta.

cards.q: The Vmax is computed as the lesser of what speeds?
cards.a: VMO, MMO, VLE or VFE.

cards.q: What symbol/bug indicates the speed in which the flaps can be retracted with a safe margin?
cards.a: The magenta F bug.

cards.q: The tip of the airspeed trend vector points to the projected airspeed/Mach in approximately what timeframe at the present rate of acceleration/deceleration?
cards.a: 10 seconds.

cards.q: What symbol/bug indicates the speed in which the airplane is trimmed for when in the landing phase?
cards.a: The TCS trim bug – a green triangle.

cards.q: Which speeds are displayed for takeoff?
cards.a: V1, VR, V2 and Vfs.

cards.q: When are the takeoff speeds automatically deselected?
cards.a: When the airplane is above 1500 feet AGL and the current airspeed is greater than the highest Vspeed + 40 kts.

cards.q: Which speeds are displayed for approach and landing?
cards.a: Vfs, Vac, Vapp and Vref.

cards.q: What does the flap selection speed bug (green dot) indicate?
cards.a: The speed in which the flaps can be extended.

cards.q: In Normal Mode (NM) what colors are the LSA bands and what do they indicate?
cards.a: White – Vss – stability speed; Yellow – the airspeed at which the AOA limiter function activates; Red – the airspeed that corresponds with the maximum allowable AOA.

cards.q: In Direct Mode (DM), what colors are the LSA bands and what do they indicate?
cards.a: Yellow and Red. The red is where the STALL aural alert is triggered.

cards.q: The altitude trend vector is computed to predict the altitude the airplane will achieve in how many seconds (assuming a constant vertical speed)?
cards.a: 10 seconds.

cards.q: Where are ADS messages (i.e. BOTH ON ADS 1/2/3) presented to the pilot and in what color?
cards.a: In amber color on the upper right corner of the PFD.

cards.q: What type of guidance will be provided to the pilots to aid in the recovery of an unusual attitude?
cards.a: Red unusual attitude chevrons are displayed and they always point towards the horizon line.

cards.q: Where are AHRS messages (i.e. BOTH ON AHRS 1 / 2 presented to the pilot and in what color?
cards.a: In amber color on the upper right corner of the PFD.

cards.q: What is the Display Control Panel (DCP) used for?
cards.a: To select PFD formats, overlays, navigation sources and range on the displays.

cards.q: What does pushing the CVS button on the DCP do?
cards.a: Allows the synthetic vision to be put on or taken off the PFD instead of the traditional blue and brown background.

cards.q: What does pushing the FPV CAGE button on the DCP do?
cards.a: It laterally centers the flightpath vector on the PFD when selected. It is only enabled when CVS is active.

cards.q: What does pushing the ET button do?
cards.a: Starts (first push), stops (second push) and removes (third push) a timer that is visible on the upper right side of the HSI.

cards.q: What does pushing the TCAS button on the DCP do?
cards.a: It places traffic overlay information on the HSI Map.

cards.q: What does the WX button do?
cards.a: It places weather overlay information on the HSI Map.

cards.q: What does the RANGE/TILT knob allow the crew to do?
cards.a: The outer control (large knob) adjusts the range and the inner control (smaller knob) adjusts the tilt of the weather radar.

cards.q: What does pushing the FMS button do?
cards.a: Selects the FMS as the primary NAV source.

cards.q: What does pushing the V/L button do?
cards.a: Changes the primary NAV source to VOR or LOC (based on the frequency tuned).

cards.q: What is the Reversionary Switch Panel used for?
cards.a: A manual reversion of displays and sensors (ADS and AHRS) in the event of a malfunction and also an alternative means of tuning.

cards.q: How can the display brightness of the DU's be adjusted?
cards.a: By the OFF/BRT control knobs on the RSP.

cards.q: If the pilot turns off the CTR DU, what will happen to the EICAS?
cards.a: The EICAS will be reverted to both the LH and RH DU's.

cards.q: What does pushing the EICAS button on the RSP do?
cards.a: It reverts the EICAS window to the LH and RH DU's.

cards.q: What does the ATT HDG button on the RSP do?
cards.a: It manually changes the AHRS source on the PFD.

cards.q: What does pushing the ADS button on the RSP do?
cards.a: It manually changes the ADS source on the PFD.

cards.q: How can the pilots interface with the avionics systems?
cards.a: Via the Multifunction Keyboard Panel (MKP) and the Cursor Control Panel (CCP).

cards.q: What is the CNCL button on the MKP used for?
cards.a: To cancel an in-process flight plan edit.

cards.q: What does pushing the FMS button on the MKP do?
cards.a: Displays the FMS format on the on-side MFW of the LWR DU.

cards.q: What does pushing the ROUTE button on the MKP do?
cards.a: Displays the route window on the on-side MFW of the LWR DU.

cards.q: What does pushing the MSG button on the MKP do?
cards.a: It shows or removes the FMS message dialog box on the MFW.

cards.q: What does pushing the DEP/ARR button do?
cards.a: On the ground it shows the departures dialog box and in flight it shows the arrival dialog box.

cards.q: What does pushing the DIRECT TO button on the MKP do?
cards.a: It brings up a direct-to dialog box which is used to edit the flight plane.

cards.q: What is the SCRATCHPAD?
cards.a: It is a 24-character display used to temporarily hold keystrokes before being entered into a display entry flightplan.

cards.q: What does pushing the EXEC button on the MKP do?
cards.a: It executes a modified flight plan making it the active flight plan.

cards.q: When does the green light bar above the EXEC button illuminate?
cards.a: When there is a modified flight plan.

cards.q: What does the MEM button on the MKP provide?
cards.a: The ability to memorize formats and to recall memorized DU formats.

cards.q: What function does the CLR/DEL button perform?
cards.a: When there is data in the scratchpad it back-spaces or clears the entire scratchpad and when there is no data in the scratchpad it enters the word "DELETE" into the scratchpad.

cards.q: How can the scratchpad text be entered into the selected display entry field?
cards.a: By pressing the ENTER button.

cards.q: What does pushing the NAV button on the MKP do?
cards.a: It takes the number entered into the scratchpad and places it into the NAV radio if it fits the range of frequencies.

cards.q: What does pushing the COM button on the MKP do?
cards.a: It takes the number into the scratchpad and places it into the COM radio if it fits the range of frequencies.

cards.q: What do the arrows on the CCP do?
cards.a: They provide an alternate to the CCP trackball for positioning the cursor on the DU's.

cards.q: What does the CKLST button on the MKP display?
cards.a: A list of available checklists.

cards.q: What does the SYS button on the MKP display?
cards.a: The synoptic page.

cards.q: What synoptic pages are available to select?
cards.a: STATUS, FLIGHT CONTROLS, ECS, FUEL, ELECTRICAL, HYDRAUICS, ANTI-ICE and MISC.

cards.q: What does the CHART button do?
cards.a: Displays the chart format on the on-side MFW of the lower DU during normal operation.

cards.q: How can the cursor be maneuvered?
cards.a: Via the trackball and arrows on the CCP.

cards.q: What can the PAGE/DATA/PUSH ENTER double stack knob on the CCP be used for?
cards.a: To position scroll list comments, position the data entry cursor or change the value of various display items or selection boxes.

cards.q: What does pushing the MENU button on the CCP do?
cards.a: It brings the display menu into view on the display window where the cursor is currently located and positions it on the first menu item.

cards.q: How many ADSP's and TAT's probes are mounted on the forward fuselage?
cards.a: 4 and 2

cards.q: For normal operations, which ADS provides information for the left seat pilot PFD? The right seat pilot PFD? The SFIS?
cards.a: ADS 1, ADS 2, and ADS 4.

cards.q: In the event of an electrical emergency, what will provide electrical power? Which DU is available? And which ADS is available?
cards.a: The RAT, CTR DU and ADS 3.

cards.q: What does the SFIS provide?
cards.a: A third independent source of attitude angles, attitude rates, accelerations, heading and vertical speed for flight guidance and navigation when the primary flight information isn't available.

cards.q: How can the menu on the SFIS be accessed?
cards.a: By the M labeled men button on the SFIS bezel.

cards.q: What are the buttons to the left and right of the M button on the SFIS bezel used for?
cards.a: To skip over options – they are labeled UP and DOWN in the entry menu context.

cards.q: When is the SFIS full screen menu available?
cards.a: Only on the ground.

cards.q: What is the ECL?
cards.a: It's an electronic checklist which permits automation of the checklist items and can be used by the crew at any phase of flight.

cards.q: What selections are available in the dropdown menu of the CHECKLIST window (ECL)?
cards.a: INDEX, QUEUE and FCN.

cards.q: How many AHRS units are there and what are they used for?
cards.a: Three; AHRS 1 is for the left seat pilot PFD, AHRS is for the right seat PFD and AHRS 3 is used exclusively by the flight controls system.

cards.q: When will the ATT/HDG ALIGNING DO NOT TAXI flag be displayed? For how long?
cards.a: During AHRS attitude and heading alignment. Up to 10 minutes.

cards.q: Which FMS pages may GPS control and indications be seen?
cards.a: FMS INIT and FMS SENSORS pages.

cards.q: How can the expanded menus for NAV or ADF be selected on the TUNING page?
cards.a: By selecting the NAV 1, NAV 2, ADF 1 or ADF 2 Gray button.

cards.q: Where can an advanced menu of ATC/TCAS selections be found?
cards.a: By selecting the gray XPNDR/TCAS button on the TUNNING page.

cards.q: Where is the weather radar control window accessed?
cards.a: Via the WX button on the DCP.

cards.q: When is the weather radar tilt and gain automatically adjusted to provide an optimum weather picture?
cards.a: When the multi scan or AUTO is selected.

cards.q: What is the coverage range of the radar and what does it provide?
cards.a: Up to 320 NM for precipitation-related weather and up to 40 NM for precipitation-related turbulence. It provides ground mapping coverage enabling the detection of major geographical features such as cities, lakes and coastlines.

cards.q: What does the Lightning Detection System provide up to what range?
cards.a: Alerts the flight crew to the presence of thunderstorm activity by mapping the lightning surrounding the airplane within 200 NM.

cards.q: What type of navigation does the FMS provide?
cards.a: Lateral and vertical navigation enroute, terminal, non-precision approaches, LNAV/VNAV and LPV approaches and coupled lateral and vertical navigation capability with an automatic transition to ILS approaches.

cards.q: Who is responsible for keeping the FMS database updated and for the accuracy of the waypoints used in the FMS?
cards.a: The operator.

cards.q: Where can the navigation and airplane database validation check be accomplished in the FMS?
cards.a: On the FMS INIT or the FMS DB format page.

cards.q: What do colors of the FMS navigation database symbolize?
cards.a: Current selected navigation database is displayed in green, the second navigation database effective date shows in white and if the database is expired, the effective date is shown in yellow.

cards.q: Which DU's can the FMS be displayed on and under which screen format size?
cards.a: The FMS format page can be accessed on any of the four DU's under a half screen format.

cards.q: What are the various FMS format pages that can be selected?
cards.a: INIT, FLPN, SETUP, WT&BAL, TAKEOFF (TOLD), LANDING (TOLD) FLT LOG, FUEL MGMT, SENSORS, FMS DB and DEFAULTS.

cards.q: How can the various FMS format pages be accessed?
cards.a: Through the CCP MENU button on the M on the top left corner of the MFW and use the drop down menu to select the FMS under a half screen format.

cards.q: On the TAKEOFF page, what needs to be set to enable the SEND button for the FMS takeoff speeds?
cards.a: The OAT, P ALT and the RWY LENGTH.

cards.q: If the crew loads inoperative NAVAID identifiers to inhibit them from the FMS navigation, when will that list be reset?
cards.a: Upon an FMS cold start.

cards.q: The FMS can hold multiple flight plans. What are they called?
cards.a: ACT FLPN – active flight plan; SEC FLPN – secondary flight plan; MOD FLPN – modified flight plan.

cards.q: What is the difference between an ACT FLPN and a MOD FLPN?
cards.a: Active flight plans that are being edited are called modified flight plans and can be executed to become an active flight plan.

cards.q: What does the ROUTE format allow for?
cards.a: It enables creation, control and viewing of the FMS legs according to the flight plan.

cards.q: The FMS sets the lateral deviation sensitivity based on what?
cards.a: The RNP value from the navigation database.

cards.q: What does synthetic vision provide?
cards.a: A perspective view of the outside world displayed on the PFD and it creates a computerized synthetic image of the external scene topography from the perspective of the flight deck.

cards.q: May synthetic vision be used as a primary navigation source?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: Does the FMS provide OEI speeds and drift down altitude?
cards.a: No.

cards.q: The SPD knob must be set to what prior to takeoff?
cards.a: MAN.

cards.q: How can the menu on the SFIS be accessed?
cards.a: By the M labeled men button on the SFIS bezel.

cards.q: What are the buttons to the left and right of the M button on the SFIS bezel used for?
cards.a: To skip over options – they are labeled UP and DOWN in the entry menu context.

cards.q: When is the SFIS full screen menu available?
cards.a: Only on the ground.

cards.q: What is the ECL?
cards.a: It's an electronic checklist which permits automation of the checklist items and can be used by the crew at any phase of flight.

mel_notes.text: One GPS may be inop if operations don't require GPS (SVS then inop). Both inop: operations not requiring GPS, one VHF nav + one DME (or two DMEs) operative, AHRS aligned; TAWS FLTA/PDA, SVS and ADS-B OUT inop.
One FMS or one TOLD function inop: cross-check TOLD with other approved data; no intermixing; TOLD inop if VSPEED database number doesn't match AFM.
TCAS inop: deactivated, transponder 2 considered inop; transponder 2 inop makes TCAS inop.
ADS-B inop (both): only with ATC authorization, and per this MEL only to move the aircraft for maintenance; one may be inop.
TAWS GPWS/modes 1–4 inop: repairs within 2 flight-days (Cat A).
Radio altimeter inop: minimums to BARO, AT Retard and TAWS modes 1–6 considered inop, 2 flight-days.
SVS inop: disable via CVS button. ECL inop: use paper checklists.

cards.q: What is the Maximum Ramp Weight (MRW) of the Praetor 500 and Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 – 37,699 Praetor 600 – 42,990

cards.q: What is the Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) of the Praetor 500 and Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 – 37,567 Praetor 600 – 42,858

cards.q: What is the Maximum Landing Weight (MLW) of the Praetor 500 and Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 – 34,172 Praetor 600 – 37,479

cards.q: What is the Maximum Zero Fuel Weight (MZFW) of the Praetor 500 and the Praetor 600?
cards.a: Praetor 500 – 25,959 Praetor 600 – 28,660

cards.q: How are the airplane forward and aft CG limits referred to?
cards.a: In terms of % MAC.

cards.q: What FMS page provides a means to load and dispatch the airplane within CG limits?
cards.a: The WT & BAL page.

cards.q: What two sections is the FMS WT & BAL page divided into?
cards.a: Aircraft Loading and Operating Empty Weight.

cards.q: If any field on the FMS WT & BAL page is out of limits for the calculations, what color will it display?
cards.a: In yellow font.

cards.q: What items do the entry data on the AIRCRAFT LOADING page include?
cards.a: The average passenger weight, number of passengers in the zones, baggage weight and taxi fuel.

cards.q: When is the AVG PAX WT used?
cards.a: Only when the number of passengers is entered into each zone.

cards.q: What shows the current weight of the aircraft?
cards.a: The Gross Weight (GWT).

cards.q: When is the ENROUTE FUEL entry displayed?
cards.a: After the flight plan is entered.

cards.q: When does the CONFIRM button on the AIRCRAFT LOADING page become active?
cards.a: Every time the ZFW is changed due to loading changes or fuel quantity changes of more than 500 lbs. from the quantity previously confirmed.

cards.q: What is Vfs?
cards.a: Final Segment Climb Speed.

cards.q: What is the Approved Performance Software that is certified to provide takeoff, landing and EnRoute approved performance data?
cards.a: iPreflight, FMS and OPERA.

cards.q: What is the maximum crosswind component for takeoff?
cards.a: 35 kts.

cards.q: What technique should be used for crosswind landings?
cards.a: The de-crab technique.

cards.q: What is the initial pitch angle for takeoff with the flap 1 position?
cards.a: 12 degrees, (followed by pitching to flight director)

cards.q: What airspeed condition is the landing data based off?
cards.a: Vref airspeed is maintained at the runway threshold (50 ft).

cards.q: When must the ICE PROTECTION ALL tables be used for unfactored landing distances?
cards.a: If the STALL PROT ICE SPEED message is displayed.

cards.q: Which climb schedule uses a lower climb speed allowing it to get to the target altitude faster and with a lower fuel, burn?
cards.a: Climb Schedule 1.

cards.q: Describe Climb Schedule 1.
cards.a:
Praetor 500: Climb at 250 KIAS and then Mach 0.72 up to selected altitude.
Praetor 600: 250 KIAS up to 10,000 ft; Climb at 250 KIAS and then Mach 0.66 up to selected altitude.
(Two-column table flattened; check the layout on the printed page.)

cards.q: Which climb schedule uses a shallower pitch angle, which gives a lesser climb rate?
cards.a: Climb Schedule 2.

cards.q: Describe Climb Schedule 2.
cards.a: Praetor 600: Climb 250 KIAS to 10,000 ft; Climb at 250 KIAS and then Mach 0.74 to selected altitude. (Only the Praetor 600 column is printed.)

cards.q: Describe Climb Schedule 3.
cards.a: Praetor 500 and Praetor 600 (same): 250 KIAS up to 10,000 ft; Acceleration from 250 KIAS up to 300 KIAS; Climb at 300 KIAS and then Mach 0.78 up to selected altitude.

cards.q: List the two ice protection system statuses that planning tables are generated for:
cards.a: OFF (both engine and wing and horizontal stabilizer ice protection systems OFF) and ALL (both engine and wing and horizontal stabilizer ice protection systems ON).

cards.q: What load factors are published in the Maneuver Capability Altitude charts?
cards.a: Various load factors from 1.2 g up to 1.5 g.

cards.q: Describe the descent schedule that is used for planning:
cards.a:
Praetor 500 and Praetor 600 (same):
Schedule 1: Descent at Mach 0.74 then 250 KIAS down to sea level.
Schedule 2: Descent at Mach 0.78 then 300 KIAS down to 10,000 ft; Deceleration from 300 KIAS to 250 KIAS at 10,000 ft; 250 KIAS down to sea level.

cards.q: What speeds are holding tables presented for?
cards.a: Minimum drag speed and 200 KIAS.
